name: Justification by Faith Alone

objectives.text: Identify from the parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector that God forgave the man who trusted in His mercy rather than in his own goodness
Name Jesus as the One who makes sinners right with God
Recall that God forgives sinners because of what Jesus did and not because of their good works
Retell how God removed Joshua's filthy garments and clothed him in clean ones and explain how this pictures God taking away sin and giving righteousness
Define justification in your own words as God pardoning all our sins and accepting us as righteous only for Christ's sake through faith
Explain how Abraham was counted righteous by believing God's promise and why Paul uses him as the pattern for all believers
Explain justification as a legal declaration by God the judge rather than a change worked inside the believer
Compare justification as a once-for-all declaration with sanctification as a lifelong work of renewal
Describe the benefits that Paul says flow from justification, including peace with God, access to grace, and freedom from condemnation
Explain from Romans 3 how God remains just while justifying sinners through the propitiation Christ made
Analyze the double imputation in which believers' sin is counted to Christ and His righteousness is counted to them
Explain from Psalm 32 and Romans 4 how Old Testament believers such as David were justified in the same way as New Testament believers
Interpret the phrase justified by faith apart from works of the law within the flow of Paul's argument in Romans and Galatians
Distinguish Christ's active and passive obedience and explain how both together form the ground of justification
Explain why faith is the instrument and not the ground of justification
Analyze how James 2 and Paul's letters use the words faith, works, and justify and show how the Reformed tradition reconciles them
Explain how the Reformed tradition teaches that justified believers still confess sin and seek forgiveness without losing their justified status
Construct a written defense of justification by faith alone from Romans and Galatians
Evaluate the objection that justification by faith alone encourages careless living using Paul's response in Romans 6
Evaluate the Council of Trent's view of infused righteousness and faith joined with works against the Reformed doctrine of imputed righteousness
Evaluate recent reinterpretations of Paul's phrase works of the law, such as the New Perspective on Paul, in light of the texts and the Reformed confessions
Analyze the role of justification in the Protestant Reformation, including Luther's reading of Romans 1, and explain why it was called the article on which the church stands or falls

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: not guilty declaration, Jesus as the one who makes us right, forgiveness not by works, definition, legal declaration, comparison with sanctification, double imputation, faith apart from works of the law, active and passive obedience, faith as instrument, defense of sola fide, infused righteousness evaluation, and the article on which the church stands or falls, which is now a historical analysis. Merged the duplicate grade 3 imputation items into a Zechariah 3 objective and a WSC Q33 definition. Replaced 'apply the peace' with a describable objective on the benefits in Romans 5 and 8. Merged the 'faith plus works' defense into the Trent evaluation. Added Luke 18 at K, Abraham in Genesis 15, propitiation in Romans 3:23-26, OT believers per WCF 11.6, James 2 reconciliation, ongoing forgiveness per WCF 11.5, the antinomian objection with HC Q64, and the New Perspective. Corrected references by adding WLC Q71, Q73, Q77, HC Q60-64, and WCF 11.5-11.6, and by tying WSC Q35 only to the sanctification comparison.
